keep.rationale: Registration lifetime is tracked by signal identity rather than binding ownership. Overlapping owners sharing a signal can therefore lose the synchronous fence that is meant to cover the durable-write window. Callers are absent, so the frequency of shared-signal registrations cannot be established.
keep.recommendedAction: Track each binding with a unique registration token or reference count, make cleanup idempotent, and test that disposing one duplicate binding leaves the other effective.

evidence.quote: if (controller.signal.aborted) return;

keep.rationale: Disposal stops future timer ticks but does not end cancellation notifications from work already launched. A retained abort listener can consequently run after the consumer has torn down this watcher or released its lifecycle ownership. Downstream listener effects are not available in this excerpt.
keep.recommendedAction: Set a disposed flag synchronously in dispose, check it before polling and immediately after the awaited read, and add a regression test resolving a pending read with a stop intent after disposal.

keep.rationale: Application data and provider cancellation metadata share the same interpretation here. A cancellation field describing an application entity can therefore become a workflow cancellation signal. Callers relying on this predicate could discard valid output or suppress diagnostics. The false-positive return is established by the implementation; downstream handling is not included in this excerpt.
keep.recommendedAction: Restrict text-based recognition to explicitly identified adapter cancellation envelopes, preserve legacy wrappers explicitly, and add a regression test showing successful content containing domain JSON with cancelled:true is not classified as cancellation.

error instanceof Error &&
		(error.name === WORKFLOW_STOP_REQUESTED_ERROR_NAME ||
			error.message.startsWith("workflow stop requested"))
keep.rationale: A failure while requesting or processing a stop can be indistinguishable from the intentional stop sentinel. Consumers that use this classifier to suppress expected cancellation errors can consequently hide an operational failure. No consumer is supplied, so the downstream consequence remains unverified.
keep.recommendedAction: Prefer the explicit stop sentinel. If legacy message-only errors must remain supported, compare against the exact expected-run message without overriding conflicting error names. Add regression tests for similarly prefixed operational failures and WorkflowStopPending errors.

keep.rationale: Cancellation before controller output exists and failures with unavailable controller artifacts lose their failed/interrupted semantic outcome. An existing synthesized artifact can also override those outcomes because controller success and artifact currency are not checked here. Although engineStatus remains accurate, consumers relying on semanticStatus receive a contradictory completion-labelled or successful-looking result and can misreport termination or omit recovery.
keep.recommendedAction: Preserve failed/interrupted semantic outcomes before applying completion-derived dynamic refinements. Keep controller/output metadata extraction separate from status precedence. Add regression cases for absent, unreadable, and synthesized artifacts, including completed-run controls.
